steps.text: The kubelet monitors resources like memory, disk space, and filesystem inodes on your cluster's nodes.
When the monitored resource levels reach specific thresholds, the kubelet can proactively fail one or more pods to reclaim resources and prevent starvation. This is known as node-pressure eviction.

The kubelet sets the phase for selected pods to `Failed`, and terminates them to reclaim resources. Node-pressure eviction does not respect pod-disruption-budgets or terminationGracePeriodSeconds, but it can use a grace period of 0s (immediate shutdown) if hard thresholds are used.

The kubelet attempts to reclaim node-level resources before terminating end-user pods. For example, it removes unused container images when disk resources are starved. If the static pod is under resource pressure and has a low priority, the kubelet may not be able to make room for that static pod.

To tune node-pressure eviction, you can adjust the thresholds used by the kubelet to determine when pods should be evicted. You can also set the grace period for terminated pods and manage resource usage through your workload management objects (like StatefulSet or Deployment).

steps.text: Ensure your PostgreSQL deployment includes a persistent volume to store the `pg_wal/` directory, which is where WAL files are archived.

Configure the archive command or library in PostgreSQL's configuration file (`postgresql.conf`) to ensure it can keep up with the average rate of your server generating WAL data. The archive should be able to handle up to 64-character long filenames and preserve both relative path (`%p`) and file name (`%f`).

Set `archive_timeout` in `postgresql.conf` or on the server command line, with a value of a minute or so. This parameter can only be set for streaming replication if you want data to be copied off the primary server more quickly.

Enable recovery by creating a file called `standby.signal` in your PostgreSQL data directory, which will allow the server to enter standby mode and continue recovery even after reaching the end of archived WAL. This is useful for high availability and read scalability.

Set `recovery_prefetch`, `wal_decode_buffer_size` and `maintenance_io_concurrency` in your PostgreSQL configuration file to optimize I/O performance during recovery, ensuring that blocks are prefetched as needed. These settings can be adjusted based on the specific workload of your database.
